soundness_flags.label: symbols and all statements/definitions using q as a treatment-period vector
soundness_flags.one_line: The core declares qvec as the indicator vector and q as its scalar limit, but D=dq^top, t1=q^topq, F^topq, bS=q⊙b, and related formulas use q as a vector; replace these occurrences with qvec and reserve q for the limit.

soundness_flags.label: thm:absorption-law and thm:subcritical-no-absorption
soundness_flags.one_line: Their probabilistic conclusions inherit thm:uniform-profile's compact h range induced by theta∈[-K,K], yet are stated over unrestricted compact subsets of Gstab and additionally invoke h→∞; separate the deterministic h→∞ profile expansion from the bounded-local-experiment stochastic theorem or state the required range.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:uniform-profile, thm:absorption-law, thm:wald-failure, and thm:masked-coverage
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Exact orthogonality to the baseline factor spaces and exact block masking are accepted as an oracle benchmark regime, not as an observable enterprise-zone implementation claim.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All full-sample-versus-masked conclusions are conditional on the stated exact-oracle block design; approximate residualization and ordinary baseline-confounding bias remain outside scope.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:absorption-law and thm:wald-failure
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The absorption and coverage claims intentionally exclude genuine ties in the deterministic profile.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The stated limits hold conditional on membership in the stable-singleton geometry Gstab; tie classification and drift-indexed selection remain the explicitly retained OEQ.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies identification, consistency, and limiting distributions of interactive-effects estimators with large N and T.
Under its maintained assumptions, the limiting distribution is invariant to fitting at least the true number of factors.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Multivariate Analysis 111 (2012), author-hosted journal PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper concerns finite-rank perturbations of large rectangular random matrices and gives singular-value/vector transitions governed by a limiting-transform threshold.

The paper studies IFE with linearly factor-structured treatment-effect heterogeneity, finds possible failure to recover ATT through bad-control absorption, and notes that methods excluding treated post-treatment cells avoid that problem.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Political Economy version of record, 2026
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and introductory description of the bias-aware minimax-linear procedure
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proposes bias-aware intervals valid uniformly over factor strength and documents bias and size distortion of conventional procedures with weak factors.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v5, August 2021; corroborating version because the cited JASA version is subscriber-restricted
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The authors propose tall-wide factor imputation and state normal distribution theory for average and individual ATT effects; exact published theorem numbering was not inspected from the JASA version.

Add a theorem placing the local profile on a common parameter path with CardosoFermanFernandes2026's strong-factor endpoint, explicitly showing how the local branch limits connect to that endpoint under matched assumptions.
Extend the oracle comparison to quantified approximate orthogonality, with an explicit residualization-error remainder that identifies when the phase law and masked coverage remain robust.
